location_description: The tension-clamp aluminum tube is located within the blue box in the center of the image and is inclined from the lower left to the upper right. Its left end is connected to the left attachment point through the steel anchor and connecting fitting, while its right end is connected to the stranded conductor extending outside the blue box.
left_end_crimp: Yes | The left end of the aluminum tube is cylindrical, with a smooth surface profile and no continuous edges or regularly flattened section. The local profile variation near the connection is insufficient to be identified as a crimping mark.
right_end_crimp: No | A continuous flat crimping surface and a clear longitudinal edge are visible near the conductor at the right end of the aluminum tube. A distinct morphological transition exists between this section and the cylindrical section on the left, which is consistent with a polygonal section formed by crimping rather than merely a highlight or shadow on the surface.
grade_result: Else | The left end of the aluminum tube remains smooth and cylindrical, whereas a distinct flat, angular crimped section is present at the right end, forming an uncrimped-crimped condition. According to the decision tree, the right end is inspected after the left end is determined to be a smooth cylindrical area. Because crimping marks are present at the right end, the defect is graded as Else.
